 Colorado voters reject mail ballot ID requirements
 By Thelma Grimes 
 Published November 3, 2026 10:25pm 
 + 
 Add The Gazette on Google
 Steve Gurr fills out test ballots during a Logic and Accuracy test to ensure all voting software and systems are functioning properly and counting accurately ahead of the Nov. 3, 2026 General Election on Friday, Oct. 9, 2026.
(Stephen Swofford, Denver Gazette) 
 The proposal to require citizens to show identification in order to vote by mail has failed in Colorado, according to the Associated Press.
 Amendment 84 asked voters to approve new identification requirements for mail ballots in the Colorado constitution. If approved by voters, the amendment requires voters who return a ballot by mail to provide identifying information, including the last four digits of their Social Security number, a driver’s license or their REAL ID number.

 Amendment 84 failed with 36% of the vote, compared with 63% opposed, according to unofficial results.
 The initiative comes amid a national debate over election security and voter verification .
 ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT 
 Under current Colorado law, voters who cast ballots by mail verify their identity by matching signatures. Election officials compare signatures on ballot envelopes with signatures already on file in state records. Colorado also requires identification for in-person voting, while first-time mail voters must provide a copy of an approved identification document.
 Supporters argued that requiring additional identifying information would strengthen election security and help prevent fraudulent ballots. Opponents contend that Colorado’s election system is already secure and warn the new requirements could create barriers for eligible voters.
 Because the proposal would amend the Colorado Constitution, it must pass with at least 55% of the vote.
